The criteria are: (1) support for a fixed task DAG as input with durable state and check-pointing; (2) deterministic, reproducible execution without autonomous planning or dynamic sub-agent generation; (3) pluggable per-node model selection to operate on the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier; (4) structured output capability available on demand rather than as a hard dependency; (5) isolation between the core routing loop and the outer validation environment; and (6) benchmark instrumentation covering per-node scoring, cost, and critical-path latency.

DeepAgents (source_001) is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph and serves as the fixed-DAG execution harness with autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation disabled. This maps directly to criteria 1 and 2. Because it sits on LangGraph (source_002), it inherits explicit nodes/edges, durable state, and check-pointing, which are necessary for reproducible per-node routing experiments. Its main tradeoff is coupling to the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem, which may constrain alternative tool abstractions.

Pydantic AI (source_003) contributes typed tool definitions and structured outputs. It is not a core dependency in v0.1 and would only be introduced if structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck. Tradeoff: it adds typing rigor and parse reliability but increases dependency surface; keeping it optional preserves a minimal core.

DeepSeek Harness / DSH (source_004) offers a pluggable agent loop and is deliberately reserved for the outer validation environment, not the core routing loop. RefractRouter v0.1 Platform Selection for 2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Routing

Executive Summary

RefractRouter v0.1 selects DeepAgents on LangGraph as the core fixed-DAG execution harness, holds Pydantic AI in reserve for structured-output needs, and confines DeepSeek Harness (DSH) to the outer validation environment [source_001][source_002][source_003][source_004]. This split targets per-node model selection to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier while keeping the system under test free of harness contamination [source_005][source_006]. The benchmark design mandates per-node scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency [source_007][source_008].

Background

Most LLM routing research chooses a single model per request, leaving per-node selection inside a task DAG underexplored [source_005]. RefractRouter treats static task decomposition as an application-layer concern and passes a fixed DAG to the router, deferring dynamic re-splitting until node-level routing is validated [source_006]. The benchmark design requires fixed DAGs, multiple candidate models, and reproducible runs small enough to re-execute [source_007].

Selection Criteria

Six criteria drive the choice: (1) fixed task DAG input with durable state and check-pointing; (2) deterministic execution with autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation disabled; (3) pluggable per-node model selection; (4) optional structured outputs; (5) isolation between the routing loop and the outer validation environment; and (6) benchmark instrumentation for per-node scoring, cost, and critical-path latency [source_005][source_006][source_007]. The scoring rubric weights coverage, evidence, depth, structure, and HTML validity [source_008].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph and is used as the fixed-DAG execution harness with autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation disabled, satisfying criteria 1 and 2 [source_001]. LangGraph contributes explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing needed for reproducible per-node routing [source_002]. Pydantic AI offers typed tools and structured outputs and is kept optional until parsing becomes a bottleneck [source_003]. DSH provides a pluggable agent loop but is reserved for the outer validation environment to avoid contaminating the system under test [source_004].

Risks

DeepAgents couples RefractRouter to the LangChain and LangGraph ecosystem, which may constrain alternative tool abstractions [source_001]. Treating static decomposition as application-layer means dynamic re-splitting is deferred, so evolving requirements could force a later redesign [source_006]. Confining DSH to the outer validation environment prevents it from acting as the router, wasting its planning autonomy inside v0.1 [source_004].

Conclusion

DeepAgents on LangGraph is selected as the core harness for correctness and reproducibility, Pydantic AI is held in reserve for structured-output needs, and DSH is confined to outer validation [source_001][source_002][source_003][source_004]. This split minimizes contamination risk while preserving the instrumentation needed to measure quality, cost, and critical-path latency on the Pareto frontier [source_005][source_007][source_008].

References

  1. DeepAgents. Claim: DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph and is used as the fixed-DAG execution harness for RefractRouter v0.1, with autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation disabled.
  2. LangGraph. Claim: LangGraph is a graph state machine framework supporting explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing, and RefractRouter uses it as the lower-level execution substrate for a fixed task DAG.
  3. Pydantic AI. Claim: Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs and is not a core dependency of RefractRouter v0.1 unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck.
  4. DeepSeek Harness. Claim: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is an agent harness with a pluggable agent loop and is reserved for the outer validation environment of RefractRouter v0.1, not the core routing loop.
  5. LLM routing research gap. Claim: Existing LLM routing work mostly selects one model for an entire request, whereas RefractRouter studies per-node model selection within a task DAG to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier.
  6. Task decomposition boundary. Claim: Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer; the router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection, with dynamic re-splitting deferred until node-level routing is validated.
  7. Benchmark design. Claim: A useful routing benchmark requires fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency, and should stay small enough to reproduce.
  8. Scoring rubric. Claim: The v0.1 scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure and readability, and HTML validity, and scoring prompts and rubric versions must be versioned with run records.
